record.title: source_dir overlap guard compares resolved path strings case-sensitively; on a case-insensitive WSL2 drvfs data dir a case-variant source_dir may bypass it and re-expose the run-2 N-4 human-token copy
record.description: SandboxManager.create (sandbox.py:398-405) resolves source_dir with Path.expanduser().resolve() and rejects it only if src == d, d in src.parents, or src in d.parents for d in {settings.home.resolve(), db_path.resolve().parent}. On Linux, resolve()/posixpath.realpath only follows symlinks and keeps the caller's spelling, and PurePosixPath equality is case-sensitive, so the guard is a pure string decision with no (st_dev, st_ino) or samefile check. v06 reproduced this independently in the sbx sandbox with a fake Docker client: exact, trailing-slash, '..', ancestor and descendant spellings were refused, but '/scratch/ci/C/users/me/proj', '.../users/me/proj/data' and '/scratch/ci/C/USERS/ME/PROJ' were accepted and passed unchanged to the /source bind mount (agents/v06/artifacts/guard_v06.out). That only shows that the string guard accepts the variant. On this case-sensitive kernel the variant is a separate stand-in directory, so the alias itself was not observed. README.md:17 lists Windows WSL2 as supported, and Settings.home defaults to ./data resolved from the server's cwd (config.py:29). If the data dir sits on a drvfs mount (/mnt/<drive>) under parent directories without the per-directory case-sensitivity flag, a source_dir that differs only in letter case (for example the project dir containing ./data, typed or cd'ed with different case and then passed through cli.py:136 os.path.abspath) would name the same directory. The guard would accept it, the daemon would bind-mount it read-only at /source, and the root setup 'cp -a /source/. /workspace/ && chown -R 1000:1000 /workspace' (sandbox.py:421-422, container has DAC_OVERRIDE/CHOWN) would copy the 0600 human_token (config.py:94-99) and agentbox.db into agent-owned /workspace. That is the run-2 N-4 escalation from the lowest-trust principal (the agent token / prompt-injected agent) to full human authority. The trigger is human_only (api.py:152) or a '*'-scope browser session (web.py:161-164 via screen_human, api.py:126-132), so this is a bypass of an operator-mistake safety control, not an attacker-chosen input; an agent cannot set source_dir. The compose deployment fails safe because its control plane sees only /var/lib/agentbox. macOS is not a supported platform per README, so the original macOS/APFS claim is dropped. Same root cause also covers other non-symlink aliases (e.g. bind mounts). Suggested fix: decide overlap on filesystem identity, i.e. reject when any of src and its ancestors is os.path.samefile with a protected dir, or any of a protected dir and its ancestors is samefile with src, instead of comparing Path strings.
record.claimed_root_cause: Overlap containment in SandboxManager.create is decided on resolved, case-preserving path strings (Path ==, .parents membership) instead of filesystem identity (st_dev, st_ino / samefile). Where two spellings name one directory, as on case-insensitive WSL2 drvfs lookups, the guard does not recognise the data directory or its ancestors.

trace.scope: create_sandbox (POST /sandboxes, human_only); also web.py:161 POST /ui/sandboxes via screen_human ('*' scope)
trace.description: Human operator (API/CLI or full-scope browser session) submits source_dir. The CLI sends os.path.abspath(source), which keeps the spelling of $PWD (cli.py:136). Agent tokens and desktop-scoped sessions cannot reach this route.
Forwards source_dir unchanged to SandboxManager.create after audit logging.
src = Path(source_dir).expanduser().resolve(): follows symlinks only and keeps the caller's letter case (verified: realpath returned the lowercase variant).
src == d / d in src.parents / src in d.parents against home and DB dir are case-sensitive string comparisons. A case-variant spelling matches no arm and is accepted (reproduced with fake Docker).
The accepted variant string becomes the read-only bind source at /source. Whether the daemon resolves it to the same inode as the data dir depends on the host filesystem (unobserved).

Root 'cp -a /source/. /workspace/' plus chown -R 1000:1000 (sandbox.py:422) with DAC_OVERRIDE copies every file under /source, including a 0600 human_token and agentbox.db if the alias holds, into agent-owned /workspace.

evidence.description: Protected set is {settings.home.resolve(), settings.db_path.resolve().parent}; no samefile/st_ino/casefold anywhere in create() (checked via inspect in harness).
Path ==/.parents comparison is case-sensitive on POSIX (PurePosixPath('/a/Users') != PurePosixPath('/a/users')).
expanduser().resolve() keeps the caller's case; only symlinks are canonicalised.
Accepted src string is the bind-mount source for /source (ro).
Root cp -a /source/. /workspace/ then chown -R 1000:1000 (line 422); container has CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE/CHOWN (line 382).
AGENTBOX_HOME defaults to ./data resolved against the server cwd, so a project dir often contains the data dir.
human_token lives in settings.home and is written 0600 (line 99); root copy ignores this.
CLI create sends os.path.abspath(source), which keeps the shell's spelling of the path.
screen_human requires scope '*', so only full human sessions reach POST /ui/sandboxes; agents cannot choose source_dir.
Supported platforms: Linux or Windows WSL2 with Docker. WSL2 /mnt/<drive> drvfs lookups are case-insensitive in directories without the per-directory case-sensitivity flag.

sbx harness (fake Docker): exact/trailing/'..'/ancestor/descendant spellings REFUSED; lowercase and uppercase variants ACCEPTED and passed to the bind mount. Run on a case-sensitive FS with a stand-in directory, so the alias is not demonstrated.

blockers: No case-insensitive filesystem exists in this container/kernel (no casefold ext4, no vfat/ntfs/drvfs mount can be created), so v06 could not observe a case-variant source_dir naming the same inode as the data dir. That is the decisive step; only the string-level guard acceptance was reproduced.

Deployment fact: whether any real agentbox install keeps AGENTBOX_HOME (or the AGENTBOX_DB directory) under a WSL2 drvfs path (/mnt/<drive>/...) whose ancestor directories are case-insensitive (no per-directory case-sensitivity flag). The default ./data under a Windows-hosted project is plausible but unobserved.

Whether the Docker daemon used with WSL2 (Docker Desktop WSL integration or native dockerd in the distro) resolves the case-variant bind source to the same directory, so that root cp -a copies the real human_token into /workspace (the copy behaviour itself is source-evident and was observed live for exact-path overlap in run-2 N-4).

validation_plan.local: On an isolated disposable Linux host with root and Docker (not this container), run: truncate -s 64M /tmp/ci.img && mkfs.ext4 -O casefold /tmp/ci.img && mkdir /mnt/ci && mount -o loop /tmp/ci.img /mnt/ci && mkdir /mnt/ci/cf && chattr +F /mnt/ci/cf && mkdir -p /mnt/ci/cf/Users/Me/proj. Alternatively use mkfs.vfat on the loop image and mount it with uid set to the test user. Export AGENTBOX_HOME=/mnt/ci/cf/Users/Me/proj/data with a dummy token (AGENTBOX_HUMAN_TOKEN unset so human_token is written 0600). (1) Run agents/v06/scratch/guard_v06.py adapted to these paths with the fake Docker client and assert that create('/mnt/ci/cf/users/me/proj') is ACCEPTED and that os.stat(src) has the same (st_dev, st_ino) as os.stat(home.parent). (2) With the real daemon and buildpack-deps:noble-curl, create the sandbox with the lowercase path, then as the agent call read_file /workspace/data/human_token and expect the dummy hum_ token. Delete the sandbox and unmount afterwards. Pass criterion: same inode and dummy token readable by uid 1000. Fail criterion: guard refuses or bind source differs.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a WSL2 host with Docker: in a throwaway Windows-created folder C:\Users\<u>\abx-test, confirm case-insensitivity with 'fsutil.exe file queryCaseSensitiveInfo C:\Users\<u>\abx-test' (expect disabled). cd /mnt/c/Users/<u>/abx-test and start 'agentbox serve' with default AGENTBOX_HOME=./data and a fresh dummy token. Run 'agentbox create /mnt/c/users/<u>/abx-test' (different case). Record whether creation succeeds and whether the agent token's read_file of /workspace/data/human_token returns the dummy token. Then delete the sandbox and the test folder. Do not use a production data directory or real token.
